headline: Germany cuts fossil fuel electricity by half in eight years
meta_description: Germany nearly halved fossil fuel electricity generation from 174.6 billion kWh in 2018 to 94.2 billion kWh in 2026, with renewables now powering 59% of electr…
summary_short: Germany has cut fossil fuel electricity generation in half over eight years, dramatically accelerating its shift toward renewable energy sources.
body:
Germany has nearly halved its fossil fuel electricity generation in just eight years, dropping from 174.6 billion kilowatt-hours in the first half of 2018 to 94.2 billion kWh in the first half of 2026.

This dramatic decline reveals the true story behind Germany's energy transformation: renewables now account for 59% of the country's electricity generation. The shift represents not just a reduction in coal and natural gas, but a fundamental restructuring of how Europe's largest economy powers itself.

The pace of change is particularly striking. What once seemed like a decades-long transition is happening in years, driven by investments in wind, solar, and other clean sources. Germany's experience offers a tangible model for other nations attempting similar energy transitions.
